thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming tail latency exceeding SLO in eu-west2 for production (~18:42 UTC). Auto-pager triggered.

oncall-SRE-Alex: I'm on it. paging details show spike started ~18:40 and correlates with increased SYN retransmits across nat-gateway pools.

netops-Maria: seeing packet drops on nat-gw-04/05. cpu ok, but conntrack saturation on those SNAT boxes. counts jumping fast.

eng-runtime-Jay: any recent rollout? i didn't push anything to serving in the window. checked commit history, nothing.

prod-support-Karen: customer-impact: 3 customers reported streaming stalls and partial responses, one customer-facing demo timed out. CS alerted top-tier customers.

oncall-SRE-Alex: quick telemetry: p95 ~320ms -> 780ms, p99 -> 4.1s. streaming stalls (tail tokens) increased 6x. traces show TLS handshake retries at the start of streams.

netops-Maria: running quick probe: 
```
ssh nat-admin@nat-gw-05 'ss -s; cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count; dmesg | tail -n 50'
```
conntrack_count: 65524 (limit 65536). lots of conntrack drops.

infra-bot: autoscale event: nat-gw pool node-add triggered at 18:41 UTC. Attempted to add two nodes; one failed with ENI attach timeout.

oncall-SRE-Alex: root cause hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion / conntrack saturation during cross-zone egress, causing handshake retries and tail latency. Need mitigation: 1) increase conntrack limit, 2) re-route traffic away from nat-gw-05, 3) warm additional NAT nodes.

eng-runtime-Jay: can we fallback streaming to reserve region (eu-west1) for affected customers? we have routing policy for emergency reroute. will open canary route for streaming endpoints to eu-west1.

oncall-SRE-Alex: do it. Jay, set a 5-min canary and watch error rates.

eng-runtime-Jay: executing runbook snippet: 
```
# add canary routing rule
redwoodctl route create --name emergency-eu-west1 --match path:/v1/streaming --priority 5 --origin eu-west1 --percent 20
```
applied. traffic shift ~20% to eu-west1. monitoring now.

prod-support-Karen: informing customers: sent note to affected customers with workaround and ETA ~30m. Logged case IDs: CS-8421, CS-8423.

netops-Maria: temporary conntrack bump on nat-gw-05: 
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
```
conntrack_count stabilized but drops persisted for a minute.

oncall-SRE-Alex: good. also disabling NAT pool affinitization to reduce stickiness to problematic nodes. Maria, proceed when ready.

netops-Maria: done. removed session affinity on pool. new connections spread across nodes. SYN retransmit rate dropping. p99 down to ~1.2s.

sre-rotate: question — why did conntrack jump so fast? any user traffic pattern change?

eng-runtime-Jay: initial correlation: a partner streaming batch job started ~18:39 from a partner IP range ~54.*.*.* creating many short-lived connections. logs show many ephemeral port reuse.

customer-success-Liu: that partner is a high-volume integration for 3rd-party analytics — they're been running large fanout tests this week. CS had warned them about burst rate but not this pattern.

oncall-SRE-Alex: mitigation summary: increased conntrack, disabled nat affinitization, shifted 20% streaming traffic to eu-west1, warmed two additional nat nodes and succeeded in ENI attach after 3 retries.

infra-bot: ENI attach log: nat-node-07 attached at 18:46 UTC.

oncall-SRE-Alex: current metrics: p95 ~260ms, p99 ~430ms, streaming stalls back to baseline. marking page as mitigated. continue to monitor for 30m.

prod-support-Karen: reopened CS tickets with mitigation notes and asked for postmortem with follow-up actions.

netops-Maria: action items: 1) increase default conntrack limit on nat pool hosts to 100k, 2) implement alert for conntrack utilization at 60%, 3) add backpressure signal to serving to reject sudden fanout bursts.

eng-runtime-Jay: runtime action items: 1) implement quick client-side exponential backoff for partner SDKs, 2) add transient retry bucketing to avoid mass reconnect storms (ticket INF-3482).

oncall-SRE-Alex: customer-impact note: 3 customers degraded, 2 customers had timeouts >10s, no data loss reported. CS outreach in progress.

sre-rotate: logging: saved tcpdump snippet for postmortem: 
```
# capture 30s of traffic on nat-gw-05
tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/nat05-handshake-surge.pcap -c 20000
```
file archived to s3://redwood-incident-archives/5360001234/pcap

customer-success-Liu: customers acknowledged and now observing recovery. one asked for a timeline on preventing reoccurence.

oncall-SRE-Alex: next steps: 1) followup postmortem documenting root cause, timeline, and permanent mitigations (conntrack default bump, routing throttles, partner rate-limit policy). 2) coordinate with Partnerships to throttle partner test runs. 3) run a chaos test to validate nat autoscaling under similar fanout.

eng-runtime-Jay: i'll draft the postmortem and include telemetry dashboards + playbook snippets.

oncall-SRE-Alex: thanks everyone. marking thread resolved but will update when postmortem is posted. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status -> MITIGATED. Incident ID: INC-2026-0423-78. Metrics attached: link to dashboard https://console.redwood.ai/d/streaming/slo-incident-5360001234
